Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

focus verb

concentrate (on)

also concentrate, focus on, concentrate on, keep your mind on, concentration

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.46 (Lewis & Short): parum dēfīgunt animōs et intendunt in ea quae perspicua sunt

animum intendere

verb phrase; intendō, third conjugation; with ad or in and the accusative, or the dative

concentrate, fix one’s mind (on)

Lewis & Short: “to direct one’s thoughts or attention to any thing”.

Other words

  • intentus, intenta, intentum — focused on, intent on

    adjective (participle of intendō); with the dative · also used · classical · Liv. 3.26.9: operī … agrestī intentus; Verg. A. 7.380: intentī lūdō

  • animum dēfīgere — fix one’s mind (on)

    verb phrase; dēfīgō, third conjugation; with in and the accusative · also used · classical · Traupman 295: animum in aliquid dēfīgere; Cic. Ac. 2.46 (Lewis & Short)

  • incumbō, incumbere, incubuī, incubitum — throw oneself into, apply oneself to

    verb, third conjugation; with in or ad and the accusative, or the dative · also used · classical · Tac. Dial. 3 (Lewis & Short): tōtō pectore novae cōgitātiōnī

    Lewis & Short: “to bend one’s attention to, to apply or devote one’s self to”.

  • hoc agere — mind what one is doing

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 350: quīn tū hoc age

    Lewis & Short s.v. agō: “to give attention to, to attend to, to mind, heed”; Hoc age! is “concentrate!”.

  • focus, focī m. — hearth, fireplace

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · M-O s.v. focal point, focus (in optics); Traupman 123, 315

    Classically the hearth (see hearth); the sense of a focal point goes back to Kepler (1604), as Morgan–Owens notes.

Examples

  • seu fossam fodiēns pālae innīxus seu cum arāret, operī certē, id quod cōnstat, agrestī intentus

    Whether he was digging a ditch, leaning on his spade, or ploughing, he was certainly, as everyone agrees, intent on his farm work.Liv. 3.26.9

  • ceu quondam tortō volitāns sub verbere turbō, quem puerī magnō in gȳrō vacua ātria circum intentī lūdō exercent

    like a top spinning under the twisted whip, which boys, intent on their game, drive in a wide circle round the empty hallsVerg. A. 7.378–380

  • quīn tū hoc age

    come on, you mind what you’re doingTer. Ph. 350

See also pay attention!, listen carefully, attend, hearth.
